title: Keep favorable cold tables separate from severe physical stress cases
statement: An X2 fault at T/4 of the simple pulse gives conditional phase error about .499920 from only the inaccessible half of the main field at eta=.5. This is conditional on a fault, not the unconditional gate error or a decoder impossibility theorem. Nominal controls with 1% chi error give pZ about .00181; an unmodelled detuning .01chi gives about .00221, retaining emitted fields and residual modes. Initial thermal overlap is 1/det[I+Nth(I-M)] for the complete passive system-field relative isometry. Three initial mean occupations .001 give pZ about .0006718, and .01 gives about .00665. A sole-main warm bath contributes 2.50686*n_in at first order for T=8; its higher-order remainder is unbounded and its assignment-error change uncomputed. Neither belongs in the cold CNOT table. Six independently prepared thermal modes have a separate conservative half-diamond envelope 1-(1+nbar)^-6. Cooling must precede loading unknown data or use actual decoupling. A dispersive interaction plus ordinary drive leaves extra state-dependent frequency and Stark terms and does not automatically supply the assumed longitudinal force.
